parts.content:
# Dialog — markup contract (the design ↔ behavior seam)

This file is the **shared vocabulary** between the behavior layer (machine + connectors,
which *set* these attributes) and the design layer (`core/design/dialog.css`, which
*styles* them). It is a human-readable spec — **not** a code dependency. Neither layer
imports the other; they meet only here (behavior-layer-design.md §2).

## Parts (`part="…"`)

| Part      | Element role                                  | Notes |
|-----------|-----------------------------------------------|-------|
| `overlay` | Full-viewport backdrop behind the dialog      | Click-to-dismiss is a connector concern, not styling. |
| `content` | The dialog surface / panel                    | Carries `role="dialog"` + `aria-modal="true"`; a flex COLUMN that height-bounds (`max-height:80vh`) and CLIPS (`overflow:hidden`); receives `resize`/dimensions when `ctx.resizable`. It is **not** the scroll container — `body` is. |
| `title`   | The dialog heading                            | Referenced by `aria-labelledby` from `content`. The core dialog's pinned HEADER zone (`flex:none`), so it never scrolls with the body. |
| `body`    | The single scroll region                      | The **only** scroll container: `flex:1; min-height:0`. Overflow is driven by `data-scroll` (see config surface). The header (`title`/`brandHeader`) and `footer` are siblings OUTSIDE it, so they stay pinned while it scrolls (sticky-header behavior). |
| `footer`  | Optional pinned controls row                  | `flex:none`, sits below `body`; stays put while `body` scrolls. |
| `close`   | The close affordance (button)                 | Wired to the `CLOSE` event by the connector. |

## State attribute (`data-state="…"`)

Behavior emits the current FSM state outward via `data-state` on `overlay` and `content`:

| `data-state` | Meaning                                                        |
|--------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| `open`       | Dialog is open (FSM state `open`).                             |
| `closed`     | Dialog is closed (FSM state `closed`).                         |

> The §1.3 contract names `data-state ∈ {open, closed}` as the canonical pair the design
> layer must handle. `CLOSE` transitions `open` → `closed` synchronously: the connector
> realises the focus-release + scroll-unlock (declared as `open`'s exit actions) via React
> effects keyed on the open state, so no transient closing-animation state is needed. (An
> earlier build routed `CLOSE` through an `animatingOut` state gated on a CSS `animationend`
> that never fired — leaving the dialog stuck open; that dead state has been removed.)

## Config surface (drives attributes / inline style, not new parts)

- **scroll / no-scroll** — `ctx.scrollable`: the (thin) connector reflects it onto a
  `data-scroll` attribute on the `body` part — `data-scroll="scroll"` vs
  `data-scroll="no-scroll"`. `core/design/dialog.css` turns that into the body's overflow:
  `scroll → overflow:auto` (scrolls on overflow), `no-scroll → overflow:clip` (clipped, no
  scrollbar and no programmatic scroll even when content overflows). Driving overflow on the
  `body` region — not the whole `content` surface — is what keeps the header pinned and makes
  the config observable in the natural un-resized state.
- **resizable + dimensions** — `ctx.resizable` / `ctx.width` / `ctx.height`: connector emits
  inline `resize/overflow/width/height` on `content` only when `canResize(ctx)` is true.
- **open / close** — the `OPEN` / `CLOSE` events on the machine (`closed` ⇄ `open`).

## Accessibility baseline (borrowed from Radix's API shape, not its delivery)

- `content`: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby` → the `title` id.
- Focus is trapped on `open` (`trapFocus`) and released on close (`releaseFocus`) — declared
  as entry/exit action names in `machine.js`; each connector performs them for its own DOM.
